editorial.exam_day_guidance: Report to your designated test center or join the online proctored session with your admission notice and a valid state photo ID or driver's license. Arrive on time as late arrivals receive no extra time.

faq.answer_text: The proctored examination typically consists of 80 to 100 multiple-choice, objective questions carefully developed by the expert CCHP Board of Trustees to test your knowledge.
faq.question_title: How many questions are on the exam?

faq.answer_text: Candidates receive email results indicating only a pass or fail status within approximately two weeks following their test date. Be sure to check with NCCHC for specific scoring threshold details.
Candidates are given a total duration of 120 minutes to complete the proctored multiple-choice examination within the allotted test window period without receiving any extra time extensions.

Applicants must hold appropriate credentials and a current, active, full, and unrestricted license or registration from a state, the District of Columbia, Puerto Rico, a U.S. territory, or Canada, along with good character and fitness.
faq.question_title: What are the eligibility requirements for the CCHP certification?

methodology.summary: This overview was built using verified facts from official NCCHC guides, candidate handbooks, and documentation regarding correctional health care standards and exam structures.

editorial.overview: The NCCHC Certified Correctional Health Professional (CCHP) certification examination assesses knowledge of nationally recognized standards and guidelines for correctional health care. Certified by the National Commission on Correctional Health Care, the assessment covers seven distinct domains including governance, patient care, medical-legal issues, and specialized health services within correctional facilities across the nation. Candidates have 120 minutes to complete the evaluation consisting of 80 to 100 multiple-choice questions.
editorial.preparation_strategy: Review the official content outline and study materials provided by NCCHC to ensure complete preparation. Focus your study efforts on the seven major knowledge areas, ensuring absolute familiarity with administrative policies, infection control, patient safety protocols, and medical-legal guidelines relevant to correctional environments during your preparation.
editorial.who_should_take: Correctional health professionals from various disciplines seeking to validate their knowledge of nationally recognized standards. Candidates must hold appropriate credentials and meet character and fitness requirements established by the CCHP Board of Trustees.
